# @homeflare/* packages

> Shared TypeScript packages published to npm: typed environment parsing, actionable
> errors, an HTTP client, Cloudflare Workers helpers, and a shared toolchain config.
> Public, no auth needed. Runtime-neutral unless stated — Bun is how they are built,
> not what consumers run. Prefer these over hand-rolling, and prefer a known SDK over
> both. Versions here are authoritative; match them rather than drifting.

```sh
bun add @homeflare/kit            # or pnpm / npm — plain ESM, any runtime
bun add @homeflare/cloudflare     # only if this runs on Cloudflare Workers
bun add -D @homeflare/config      # shared tsconfig / oxlint / oxfmt
```

**Jump to what you need:** reading config → `parseEnv` · throwing or mapping an error →
`KitError` · calling an HTTP API → `client` · Cloudflare Access → `verifyAccessJwt` ·
logging in a Worker → `log` · picking a dependency version → House versions · needing
something that is not here → If something you need is missing.

## @homeflare/kit — runtime-neutral, use anywhere

```ts
import {
  parseEnv, isUnset, EnvError,                  // typed env parsing, zero deps
  KitError, kindForStatus, KIND_DESCRIPTIONS,   // actionable errors
  client, http, HTTPError, TimeoutError,        // ky-based HTTP with retries
  VERSION,
} from '@homeflare/kit';
import type {
  EnvSchema, EnvSpec, ErrorKind, KitErrorOptions, KyInstance, Options,
} from '@homeflare/kit';
```

### parseEnv — config, validated once

```ts
const cfg = parseEnv(
  {
    API_URL: { type: 'string' },
    PORT: { type: 'number', default: 8787 },
    DEBUG: { type: 'boolean', default: false },
  },
  env, // a Worker's env binding, or process.env
);
cfg.PORT; // number   cfg.DEBUG; // boolean
```

Throws `EnvError` on the first missing or malformed key, naming the KEY and never the
value. Specs are `{ type: 'string' | 'number' | 'boolean', optional?, default? }`.

⚠️ `''`, `'null'` and `'undefined'` all count as unset. An unbound workerd binding
arrives as the four-character *string* `"null"`, so code checking only for `''` sends
`Authorization: Bearer null` and gets a bare 401 that reads like a bad credential.
Values are trimmed — a rendered env file has a trailing newline.

⚠️ `'false'` parses as `false`. `Boolean('false')` is `true`, which is how a flag turned
off in a dashboard stays on in production.

### KitError — failures a caller can act on

```ts
throw new KitError('forbidden', 'token lacks Things:Read', {
  system: 'things-api',                 // ⛔ name it; "request failed" tells nobody anything
  remedy: 'ask an operator to widen the grant',
});

kindForStatus(429);  // 'rate_limited'
err.retryable;       // true only for rate_limited and upstream_unreachable
```

Kinds: `unauthenticated` · `forbidden` · `upstream_rejected` · `rate_limited` ·
`upstream_unreachable` · `bad_arguments` · `misconfigured`.

⚠️ 429 is `rate_limited`, never a kind meaning "your arguments are wrong" — that mapping
had a throttled caller rewriting a correct call until it concluded the tool was broken.

### client / http — HTTP with sane retries

```ts
const api = client(cfg.API_URL, { headers: { authorization } });
const things = await api.get('/things').json<Thing[]>();
```

Built on `ky` (zero dependencies). Retries **only idempotent methods** — POST is
excluded — 3 attempts, 10s timeout **per attempt**, so worst case is ~30s plus backoff.
Shorten both on a Worker request path. `baseUrl` resolves per the URL standard: a
leading slash is fine.

```ts
import { rateLimitAware, retryAfterMs, MAX_RETRY_WAIT_MS } from '@homeflare/kit';
const discord = client(base, rateLimitAware);   // honours x-ratelimit-reset-after
```

⚠️ Use `rateLimitAware` against any API sending `x-ratelimit-reset-after` (Discord, and
anything Discord-shaped). Measured against ky 2.1.0: `retry-after: 1` is honoured
(1006ms) but `x-ratelimit-reset-after: 1` is **ignored** (303ms — ky's own backoff). A
429 not waited out becomes a retry storm, and a storm escalates from a throttled route
to a throttled **token** — which takes down everything sharing that credential.

## @homeflare/cloudflare — Workers only

```ts
import { verifyAccessJwt, log, VERSION } from '@homeflare/cloudflare';
import type { AccessIdentity, AccessOptions, LogFields, Logger } from '@homeflare/cloudflare';

const who = await verifyAccessJwt(request, {
  teamDomain: env.TEAM_DOMAIN,   // https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com
  audience: env.POLICY_AUD,      // ⛔ never omit
});
who.email; who.sub; who.claims;

const rlog = log.with({ requestId, path: url.pathname });
rlog.info('handled', { status, ms });   // also .debug .warn .error
```

⛔ Never omit `audience`. Any Access app in the account mints a JWT the team domain will
verify; the AUD tag is the only thing saying the token was minted for THIS app.

Verification throws on a missing header, bad signature, wrong audience, or expiry —
deliberately, so a forgotten `if (!ok)` cannot become an open door.

⚠️ JWKS fetches go through a circuit breaker (`breakered`, `BREAKER_COOLDOWN_MS`),
installed at jose's own `customFetch` seam. Measured on jose 6.2.12: five verifications
against a **404ing** certs endpoint made five outbound fetches, and no `cacheMaxAge` or
`cooldownDuration` setting changes that — jose only records a timestamp on a *successful*
fetch. Without the breaker, an Access outage turns every inbound request into an outbound
one. A failing URL now latches closed for 30s, per URL.

Logging writes one JSON object per line, which Workers Logs indexes field by field. No
logging library: `console.log` of JSON *is* the integration. ⛔ Never log a credential —
there is no redaction layer, by design.

## @homeflare/config — shared toolchain

```jsonc
// tsconfig.json — an app or a Worker
{ "extends": "@homeflare/config/tsconfig.base.json" }

// tsconfig.json — a package that publishes types
{ "extends": "@homeflare/config/tsconfig.lib.json" }
```

```json
// .oxlintrc.json
{ "extends": ["./node_modules/@homeflare/config/oxlintrc.json"] }
```

⚠️ oxlint's `extends` takes **file paths**, not package names — there is no
`eslint-config-*` style resolution.

⚠️ Copy `node_modules/@homeflare/config/oxfmtrc.json` to `.oxfmtrc.json` — **with the
leading dot**. Without it oxfmt silently uses its defaults and rewrites your quotes.

## Two kinds of auth — not interchangeable

- `@homeflare/cloudflare` → **Cloudflare Access**. The edge already authenticated the
  caller; you verify its assertion. Stateless.
- `@homeflare/auth` → **Better Auth**. *You* are the identity provider: sessions,
  accounts, a database.

⚠️ Reaching for the wrong one produces a system that looks authenticated and is not.

## House versions — match these, do not drift

`typescript 7.0.2` · `zod 4.6.5` · `jose 6.2.12` · `hono 4.13.7` · `ky 2.1.0` ·
`capnweb 0.12.0` · `@cloudflare/workers-types 5.20260908.1` · `@cloudflare/kumo 2.13.2` ·
`react 19.3.0` · `better-auth 1.7.5` · `oxlint 1.83.0` · `oxfmt 0.68.0`

⛔ UI is **Kumo**, not shadcn/Radix — Kumo already occupies that layer, on Base UI. Two
primitive libraries in one app means two styling conventions and two a11y models.

## @homeflare/ui — styles and tokens, not a component wrapper

```tsx
import '@homeflare/ui/styles';                          // once, at your app root
import { Button } from '@cloudflare/kumo/components/button';
```

⛔ Kumo is **not** re-exported, deliberately: a barrel pulls all 44 components into the
module graph, so an app using a Button would ship the chart library. Import Kumo's
components directly and granularly, as Kumo documents.

⚠️ Kumo is a **peer**, so you declare it — one copy must win, or you get two stylesheets
and two Base UI instances. `@homeflare/ui/styles` is Kumo's stylesheet plus HomeFlare
tokens; it replaces `@cloudflare/kumo/styles`.

`@homeflare/auth` is still a scaffold exporting only `VERSION`.

## If something you need is missing

⛔ **Do not hand-roll a local version and move on** — that is how thirty-seven repos end
up with thirty-seven answers to one question. Check whether a known SDK does it well
first (this kit uses `ky`, `jose`, `zod` and Kumo rather than reimplementing them), then
report it under the heading `MISSING FROM @homeflare/*`, in the shape
[CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-a-gap](./CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-a-gap) gives.

⚠️ A function that exists but is the **wrong shape** counts, and so does a **version
conflict** — a silent local override becomes drift that surfaces months later in someone
else's build.
